output.summary: An aromatic, perennial evergreen creeper in the mint family, ground-ivy has no native origin specified in the supplied account and was spread worldwide by European settlers. Its square stems root where they touch the ground, forming dense mats, and release a distinctive smell when damaged.
output.edibilityNote: It has long been eaten as salad greens; pre-bloom leaves can be cooked as a vegetable or made into tea.
